title: Repeat-imaged site coverage
description: One repeat-imaged site's coverage, reduced to the facts that decide whether it is worth analysing — emitted one object per line by `umbra sites --json` and, wrapped in a list under `sites`, by the `find_repeat_sites` agent tool (MCP / LangChain / LlamaIndex). Umbra files every pass of an area under one task, so a site's coverage is how many dated passes share it; this is the discovery answer to *which* site before every `change` / `timescan` / `stack` / `pick_change_interval` verb answers *what changed there*. Every field is present on every record; the ones a site with fewer than two dated passes cannot supply are null rather than absent.

task.description: The Umbra task (site) codename every pass of this site is filed under — the argument `umbra search --area` takes to reach it.

label.description: A human-readable name: the first pass's baked place name (`umbra index bake`) when one exists, else the `task` codename. Single-sourced with the static showcase's featured-gallery label so the two cannot drift.

passes.description: How many acquisitions of this site are in the ranked pool, dated or not — the count that ranks it (more passes, more to measure).

comparable_passes.description: How many passes can actually be differenced together for change detection: the largest set of dated passes sharing one polarization — the pool a `change` / `timescan` / `stack` selection draws from before the mixed-polarization refusal the analysis verbs enforce. Undated passes are excluded (they cannot be ordered onto a time axis). Below `passes` means the raw count overstates the analysable depth (a polarization mix, or undated passes riding along); equal to the dated-pass count when every dated pass shares one polarization. `polarizations` says which polarizations are present, this says how deep the biggest comparable subset is.

first.description: The earliest pass's acquisition date, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, or null when no pass carries a datetime.

last.description: The latest pass's acquisition date, ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`, or null when no pass carries a datetime.

span_days.description: Whole days from the first dated pass to the last, or null with fewer than two dated passes (no span to measure).

min_revisit_days.description: The shortest gap in days between two consecutive dated passes — the site's tightest revisit — or null with fewer than two dated passes.

median_revisit_days.description: The median gap in days between consecutive dated passes — the site's typical cadence — or null with fewer than two dated passes.

max_revisit_days.description: The longest gap in days between two consecutive dated passes — the site's worst-case temporal resolution, the widest stretch a change could have gone unseen — or null with fewer than two dated passes. Far above `median_revisit_days` means a bursty or thinning series rather than a steady cadence.

bbox.description: The union footprint of every pass that has one, `[min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat]` in WGS84 degrees — the rectangle a follow-up `--bbox` / `--intersects` would cover — or null when no pass carries a footprint.

products.description: The product/asset types available across the site's passes (any of GEC, SICD, SIDD, CPHD), sorted.

polarizations.description: The polarizations present across the site's passes, sorted. More than one means the passes are not all comparable for change (HH and VV measure different scattering); filter to one before differencing.

hrefs.description: The site's pass STAC URLs, oldest-first (undated passes last) — the whole roster to choose passes from. Handing all of them to `umbra change` / `stack` / `pick_change_interval` trips the mixed-polarization refusal whenever `comparable_passes` is below `passes`; use `comparable_hrefs` for a selection that pipes straight onward.

comparable_hrefs.description: The subset of `hrefs` belonging to the `comparable_passes` group — the largest set of dated passes sharing one polarization, oldest-first — so it is the selection to hand `umbra change` / `stack` / `pick_change_interval` straight through without tripping the mixed-polarization refusal those verbs enforce. Its length equals `comparable_passes` (barring a pass with no URL, which `hrefs` also drops); equal to `hrefs` (minus any undated passes) when every dated pass is already comparable, empty when no pass is dated.
